description: Work through the remaining backlog in order: (1) wire the inference service into node.go and add a `matrix inference` CLI command so inference jobs run end to end (local echo backend is GPU-free/testable; provider-API/OpenAI backend reads key from env); (2) bridge burn->unlock watcher/relayer if achievable as a real, testable-against-local-hardhat daemon, otherwise implement the honest runnable piece and clearly state what an operator still runs; (3) other small real gaps (e.g. minimal web tests). Finish with an honest STILL-REMAINING list. Depends on FEAT-002.
steps: INFERENCE WIRING: In internal/node/node.go, construct inference.Service (inference.NewService with Market, a Registry, a consensus-backed Settler = n.consensus, and an Accounts resolver) after consensus is running. Provide a way to register a local inference Backend (the GPU-free echo backend in internal/inference/echo.go) for a provider. Build and start an inferenceapi.Server (internal/inferenceapi, matrix.inference.v1) on a configurable Market/Inference addr (extend node.Config with an inference addr; default e.g. 0.0.0.0:9092), gated by the same ACL auth. Add GetInference() / GetInferenceAPI() accessors and Stop() teardown. Handle the Accounts resolver honestly (document that a node holds keys for buyers it settles for; for dev, resolve from the local wallet / a provided resolver).

INFERENCE CLI: add matrix.inference.v1 client to internal/cli/client.go and a `matrix inference` command (e.g. submit --buyer --provider --prompt [--units], get --id) that drives the InferenceService RPCs. Follow job.go patterns. Add an in-process cli test against an in-memory InferenceService.

INFERENCE TESTS: add/extend node and inferenceapi tests proving the echo backend runs an inference job end to end through the node wiring (reserve -> fulfill -> settle -> completed), reusing existing inference test patterns. Run go test -race on internal/inference, internal/inferenceapi, internal/node, internal/cli.

BRIDGE WATCHER: inspect internal/bridge and contracts (WrappedMatrix.sol/bridge, Burned events). If a real watcher/relayer can be built and tested against a local hardhat node (OPEN_INTERNET; hardhat brings solc), implement an always-on watcher that ingests on-chain Burned events and drives the decoded/replay-safe burn->unlock primitive, with a test against a local hardhat chain. If full automation is not achievable in-sandbox, implement the honest runnable piece (e.g. a bridge-watch command/daemon that decodes and applies a provided/observed burn event) and clearly document in code + handback what an operator still runs.

WEB TESTS: add minimal tests for apps/web if reasonable (e.g. a lightweight test for CopyButton or a smoke test), only if it can be wired without destabilizing the toolchain; if it requires adding a test runner that risks the build, document it as a remaining item instead.

Run all verification gates: make proto; cd services/core && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...; go test -race on all touched packages; matrix CLI builds and new subcommands run; contracts npx hardhat test still green (run it); apps/web corepack yarn lint + build.
Demonstrate an inference job running end to end against a live node (echo backend) and append the transcript to the task's transcript file.

Write an honest STILL-REMAINING / NOT DONE summary into .agents/tasks/task-genesis-funding-quickstart/STILL-REMAINING.md: what could not be completed and why, what only the user can do (real mainnet deploy needs their funded key; GPU-dependent local inference beyond echo; native Tauri bundle needs system libs), and any operator-run steps for the bridge watcher.
acceptance_criteria: inference.Service + inferenceapi.Server are constructed and served by node.go (verified served, not just built), with a GPU-free echo backend registerable for a provider, and torn down in Stop().
`matrix inference` CLI command drives inference jobs end to end; an in-process cli test and a node/inferenceapi test prove reserve->fulfill->settle->completed with the echo backend.
Bridge burn->unlock: either a real watcher tested against a local hardhat node, or an honest runnable piece with clearly documented operator steps (no overstated claims).
All verification gates pass: make proto, go build/vet/test, go test -race on touched packages, contracts hardhat test green, apps/web lint+build clean.
STILL-REMAINING.md honestly lists what is not done and why.
verification: make proto && cd services/core && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...
cd apps/web && corepack yarn lint && corepack yarn build
Run a live inference job through matrixd + matrix inference (echo backend) and capture the transcript
findings:
Implemented and verified. Three commits to main (app/library code per orchestrator policy; .agents/ metadata left untracked, matching FEAT-001/002/003 convention): dc36ee5 (inference wiring + CLI), 05a22b5 (bridge burn->unlock watcher), 1533f1b (web click-to-copy inference command).

BACKLOG ITEM 1 - INFERENCE WIRING + CLI (dc36ee5):
- node.go: added Inference config (Addr default 0.0.0.0:9092, EchoProvider default 'demo-inference-provider'). After the market API starts, node constructs inference.NewService(Market=n.market, Registry=new, Settler=n.consensus, Accounts=walletAccounts) and an inferenceapi.Server gated by the SAME EnableACLs auth as marketapi, started in Start() and torn down first in Stop(). Confirmed n.consensus satisfies inference.Settler (SubmitAccountTransfer + WaitForSettlement in consensus/settle.go + engine.go). Registers the GPU-free echo backend (inference.NewEchoBackend) for the demo provider. Added GetInference()/GetInferenceAPI() accessors + RegisterInferenceAccount().
- Accounts resolver (honest): new internal/node/inference_accounts.go walletAccounts resolves buyer signing keys from (1) in-memory registrations (Add) and (2) on-disk ~/.matrix wallet files matched by public key = account id. Documents the single-operator dev-custody model; never fabricates custody. A multi-tenant deployment substitutes its own resolver.
- Initialize (matrixd --init) writes the inference addr + echo_provider into config.yaml.
- CLI: client.go gained an inferenceConn + dialInference (inference server is on its own addr, so `matrix inference` uses --inference-addr default 127.0.0.1:9092, NOT the market --addr on 9091). internal/cli/inference.go adds `matrix inference submit --buyer --provider --prompt [--model --units --fulfill]` (submits then fulfills by default = reserve->fulfill->settle->completed in one command) and `get --id`. Wired into root.go.

INFERENCE TESTS (all pass incl -race): internal/cli/inference_test.go (in-process against an in-memory inferenceapi server backed by a real consensus-settled inference.Service + echo backend; asserts completed status, echo completion, and ledger balances buyer 993/provider 7 for the deterministic 7-unit 'hello world' job; plus a get-by-id test). internal/node/inference_wiring_test.go (walletAccounts resolves from memory AND disk and the resolved key signs verifiably; and the EXACT node wiring - echo backend + walletAccounts + consensus settler - settles a job end to end with balances moving).

LIVE DEMO (inference-transcript.txt): single self-contained script (sandbox PID-namespace isolation) built matrixd+matrix, matrixd --init (echo_provider + reward_pool 1e18), started matrixd with enable_acls=false, created a buyer wallet under ~/.matrix (so the node's walletAccounts resolver holds its key), funded it 1,000,000 from the reward pool, registered demo-inference-provider on the order book, then `matrix inference submit --prompt "hello world"` returned status=completed, completion 'echo: user: hello world', units 7. Balances moved buyer 1000000->999993, provider 0->7 through consensus settlement. OpenAI/provider-API backend is env-gated (OPENAI_API_KEY); no key present, so the echo backend was exercised (noted in transcript).

BACKLOG ITEM 2 - BRIDGE BURN->UNLOCK WATCHER (05a22b5): inspected internal/bridge (Bridge.ProcessBurn is a replay-safe unlock keyed on burn id; DecodeBurnedLog/DecodeBurnEvent already turn a real WrappedMatrix Burned log into a BurnEvent, byte-verified by the existing BridgeE2E hardhat test) and WrappedMatrix.sol (event Burned(address indexed burner, string nativeRecipient, uint256 amount)). Built the always-on ingestion half that was missing:
- internal/bridge/ethrpc.go: a dependency-free Ethereum JSON-RPC client (HTTPEthClient: eth_blockNumber + eth_getLogs, net/http + encoding/json only, honoring the bridge's stdlib-only constraint) implementing an EthClient interface.
- internal/bridge/watcher.go: a polling Watcher that scans [cursor, head-confirmations] for Burned logs, decodes each via DecodeBurnedLog, applies via ProcessBurn, advances a cursor, chunks large ranges (MaxBlockSpan), stays Confirmations behind head, and treats a re-observed/already-processed burn as a benign no-op. Run(ctx) loops; Poll(ctx) does one deterministic pass.
- cmd/bridge-watch: the runnable relayer that scans a deployed WrappedMatrix over JSON-RPC and applies unlocks, printing applied burns as JSON.
- contracts/scripts/bridge-burn-emit.ts: deploys WrappedMatrix, mints from a REAL Go attestation (cmd/bridge-attest, same path as BridgeE2E), and burns to emit a Burned event, printing coordinates for the watcher.
Tests: internal/bridge/watcher_test.go (scan/apply/cursor, confirmation depth, replay-safety, JSON-RPC hex helpers) with a fake client, all pass incl -race. LIVE end to end against a LOCAL HARDHAT node (bridge-watch-transcript.txt): hardhat node -> deploy+mint+burn -> `go run ./cmd/bridge-watch` polled eth_getLogs, decoded the real Burned event, and unlocked 3 native units to the named recipient (asserted recipient + amount match). AUTOMATION BOUNDARY (honest, in STILL-REMAINING): the watcher is a single-node polling relayer; it is NOT yet wired as a matrixd subsystem (operators drive cmd/bridge-watch or a script and supply RPC URL/contract/start block), and multi-validator consensus on the unlock is a larger unshipped design item.

BACKLOG ITEM 3 - WEB TESTS: deliberately did NOT add a web test runner. apps/web has no test runner and adding jest/vitest+jsdom to Next 15 / React 19 / Tailwind v4 risks the lint/build gates the task warned against; documented as a remaining item in STILL-REMAINING.md instead. Verified apps/web lint+build stay clean.

BACKLOG ITEM 4 - SMALL SAFE GAP (1533f1b): added a click-to-copy `matrix inference submit` command block to the EXISTING /products/inference page (reusing the FEAT-003 CopyButton), accurate to the shipped CLI + echo backend. NO new route added (only an existing page modified). Orchestrator may optionally re-screenshot /products/inference to show the copy block.

VERIFICATION (all green): make proto OK; go build/vet/test ./... OK; go test -race on inference/inferenceapi/node/cli/bridge OK; matrix --help shows inference and it runs; contracts npx hardhat test 38 passing; apps/web corepack yarn install --frozen-lockfile + lint (no warnings) + build (all routes prerendered) clean; did NOT touch the @config directive in globals.css. Live transcripts captured for inference and bridge.

STILL-REMAINING.md written with the honest not-done list: real mainnet/testnet deploy needs the user's funded key (env-only); GPU/local-http and OpenAI inference backends beyond echo are env/hardware-gated; native Tauri bundle needs webkit2gtk/gtk; bridge watcher operator-run steps + the un-wired in-matrixd subsystem + multi-validator consensus unlock; web test runner intentionally deferred.

NEW WEB ROUTES NEEDING SCREENSHOTS: NONE (only the existing /products/inference page was modified). GOTCHAS: (1) inference server binds its own port 9092; the CLI inference commands use --inference-addr, not the global --addr. (2) A stray services/core/bridge-watch binary can appear from `go build ./cmd/bridge-watch/...`; it is not committed (removed). (3) Live demos must run as a single self-contained bash script due to the sandbox PID-namespace isolation (--die-with-parent); background processes do not survive across tool calls.
